info.title: Chronos API
info.description:
Plotline & timeline API for fiction writers (see docs/chronos/design.md).

Two classes of rule govern writes. **Referential** rules are hard: a bad reference, an impossible timeframe, or deleting something still in use is rejected. **Story-logic** rules (temporal conflict, plotline ordering, convergence on the terminus) are soft: the write always succeeds and the finding is reported in the book's `status` and in `GET /books/{book}/validate`.

Every response separates stored fields (editable; send them back on a write) from computed fields (`status`, `_links`, `rev`) which are read-only.

servers.description: Same origin as the chronos service

tags.name: books
tags.description: Books, their terminus, and whole-book reports

tags.name: plotlines
tags.description: Ordered threads of events within a book

tags.name: visualizer
tags.description: The read-only plotline visualiser (web UI and its read helpers)

tags.name: calendars
tags.description: The library of named, reusable calendars. Identity is (owner, id); books attach a *copy*.

200.description: Books the caller has read access to.

post.description: The creator becomes the book's owner (full permissions at book scope).

get.description: Includes the computed `status` — the one-glance answer to whether the story currently holds together.

delete.summary: Delete a book and everything in it

post.description: Sets the single event every plotline must end at. Plotlines that do not reach it are reported (soft), not rejected.

get.description: Runs every story-logic check across the whole book: temporal conflicts, plotline ordering, convergence on the terminus, and references to Akasha articles that no longer exist.
Events as nodes, 'precedes' edges from consecutive plotline members, annotated with convergence (in-degree > 1) and divergence (out-degree > 1) points.
Returns the stored record, a computed `status`, and a `_links` block. Lean by default; `?expand=events` inlines event summaries.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Inline referenced resources instead of returning bare ids.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description: Inline this plotline into every thread that continues into it, then delete.

delete.description: Blocked with `409 PLOTLINE_IN_USE` while other plotlines still continue into this one, unless `inline=true` — which absorbs this plotline into each dependent first, so their stories survive the deletion.

post.description: Every EntityRef must already exist in Akasha, or the write is rejected with 422. A temporal conflict does NOT reject the write — it is reported.

delete.description: Blocked with `409 EVENT_IN_USE` while any plotline still lists it, unless `detach=true`. Deleting the book's terminus is always blocked (`409 TERMINUS_IN_USE`) until a new one is designated.

parameters.name: detach
parameters.description: Remove the event from every plotline that lists it, then delete it.

get.summary: Plotlines converging into / diverging from an event
get.description: The event-local slice of the story graph. Incoming edges grouped by predecessor give convergence; outgoing edges grouped by successor give divergence.

parameters.name: relation
parameters.description: Return only the matching block instead of the full neighborhood.

get.description: Owners only -- ownership is holding `delete` at this scope, which the creator gets automatically. The admin role does not confer it.

200.description: Everyone granted at this exact scope.

put.summary: Invite a collaborator or change their role
put.description: Owners only. Idempotent: re-inviting replaces the existing book-scoped grant and leaves the user's Akasha grants untouched.

200.description: The collaborator's role on this book.

delete.description: Owners only. Removes their book-scoped grant.

post.summary: Absorb the continuation chain into this plotline
post.description: The inverse of adopting a continuation: copies the resolved `effective_events` into this plotline's own `events` and clears `continues_into`, so the thread keeps the exact story it had but no longer depends on another plotline. A no-op when there is no continuation, so it is safe to repeat. Refuses on a broken chain rather than inlining a partial path.

get.description: Serves the read-only web UI. Requires a session; a browser is redirected to `/login` when unauthenticated.

get.summary: Akasha worlds this writer can draw a book's cast from
get.description: Fills the world chooser in the new-book form. Alone among the `/ui` helpers this is **not** book-scoped: the writer picks a world while creating a book, when there is no book to authorize against. The only gate is therefore the Akasha one -- a world, and a category within it, is offered exactly when the caller could read something in it.

get.summary: List a book's plotlines (filtered, ordered, paginated)
get.description: A read helper for the visualiser table. Returns the book's plotlines ordered by name, narrowed to those whose name, goals, or event titles contain all the words in `filter`, one page at a time.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Space-separated words; a plotline matches only if it contains all of them.

get.description: Everything wrong across every plotline in one book, in the same words the plotline view uses, grouped by kind and ordered to be read top to bottom. `/books/{book}/validate` answers the same question for a machine — ids, categories, one ordering violation per thread; this answers it for the writer. `problems` are contradictions and are exactly what the book's `status` is computed from; `notes` are things worth knowing that are not faults (an undated scene is a draft state, not a fault).

get.summary: Read a referenced Akasha article (same-origin proxy)
get.description: A read helper for the visualiser's entity cards: fetches one Akasha article an event references, so the browser never has to talk to Akasha cross-origin. Two checks: you must be able to read the book, and you must hold Akasha `read` permission on the article itself (`403` otherwise). A dangling reference (article since deleted) reports `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: Akasha database of the referenced article.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Akasha collection of the referenced article.

post.summary: Judge a candidate plotline without saving it
post.description:
Returns the candidate judged exactly as `GET /books/{book}/plotlines/{plotline}?expand=events` would judge it once saved: its resolved path, its per-scene findings and its status. Writes nothing, and the plotline need not exist yet -- this is what lets the editor show a reorder's effect while the writer drags, without reimplementing any rule in the browser.

The result is deliberately **not** a `Plotline`: it carries no `rev` and no `self` link, because the thread it describes may not exist. Everything else is the same shape, from the same presenter.

Requires `write`, because it is an editing affordance: previewing must not succeed where saving would be refused.

200.description: The candidate, judged as if saved.

get.summary: Search the Akasha articles a scene could reference
get.description: Type-ahead for the new-scene form, proxied same-origin so the browser never talks cross-service. Matches an article's slug or title. Two gates, as with the article proxy: `read` on the book, then Akasha `read` on each result -- so the picker never suggests something Akasha would refuse to open.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What the writer has typed so far.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: Override the searched database (defaults to the one this book's scenes mostly reference).

get.summary: List a book's scenes (filtered, ordered, paginated)
get.description: The book's scenes in story order -- scheduled by time, undated last -- narrowed to those whose title, place or cast contain all the words in `filter`. Summaries only; the full record for one scene is `GET /books/{book}/events/{event}`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Space-separated words; a row matches only if it contains all of them.

get.summary: Name these ticks in the book's calendar
get.description: Formats raw ticks through the book's calendar, so the scene form can show what `240` means as the writer types it. Up to 8 per request; a non-integer `tick` is a 400.

200.description: One entry per tick, in the order asked.

get.summary: The calendar library visible to you
get.description: Your own calendars plus any shared with you. Not book-scoped: a calendar outlives any one book, and is chosen while a book is being created — when there is no book to scope to.

post.summary: Create a calendar in your library
post.description: `owner` must be you — a writer may only create under their own name. The creator owns it outright. Two writers may each hold a calendar with the same slug, and neither creation tells the other anything.

put.description: A full replace, like every other PUT here. Books that already attached this calendar are **not** re-dated: each holds its own copy, and is offered the change explicitly instead.

delete.description: Not a cascade. Books that copied it keep working — the copy *is* their calendar — and only their provenance pointer goes dangling, the same posture Chronos takes toward a deleted Akasha article. Grants naming this calendar are swept, so the slug is free again.

get.description: Owners only -- ownership is holding `delete` at this scope, which the creator gets automatically. The admin role does not confer it.

200.description: Everyone granted at this exact scope.

put.description: Owners only. Idempotent. The calendar appears in their library beside any calendar of their own that happens to share its name — they are distinct records, told apart by owner.

delete.description: Owners only. Books they already attached it to are untouched: they hold their own copy.

post.description:
Turns a date the writer typed into the ticks it names, so the scene form can echo `= Year 3, Month 4, Day 12 -> ticks 19704 -> 19728` while they type. The inverse of `GET /books/{book}/ui/ticks`.

A POST for a read, like `ui/plotline-preview`: a date is a nested object and there are two of them, which a query string says badly. It writes nothing and needs only `read`.

The arithmetic lives here rather than in the browser so that client and server cannot disagree about what a date means. Shares its parsing with the real write, so a timeframe this accepts is one `PUT .../events/{event}` will accept.

200.description: The ticks the dates name, dated back again.

sessionCookie.name: session
sessionCookie.description: Signed session cookie from `POST /login` on either service. Chronos and Akasha share one SECRET_KEY, so a single login covers both.

PlotlineId.name: plotline
PlotlineId.description: Plotline id (slug), unique within the book.

EventId.name: event
EventId.description: Event id (slug), unique within the book.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Optimistic-concurrency precondition — the `rev` you last read, e.g. "3". Omit (or send `*`) for an unconditional write. A stale value returns 409.

CalendarOwner.name: owner
CalendarOwner.description: The account that keeps this calendar. Half of its identity: two writers may each keep a calendar with the same slug.

CalendarSlug.name: calendar
CalendarSlug.description: Calendar id (slug), unique within its owner's library.

CalendarView.name: calendar
CalendarView.description: Which of the book's attached calendars to write dates in. Omit for its primary (first) one. A calendar the book has not attached is a 404, never a silent fallback — a stale choice must say so rather than mislabel every date in the response. Ticks stay canonical: this chooses how they are *said* -- and, on a write carrying `start_date`/`end_date`, which reckoning those dates are read in.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but lacking the required permission on this book (`FORBIDDEN`).

NotFound.description: No such book, plotline or event (`BOOK_NOT_FOUND`, `PLOTLINE_NOT_FOUND`, `EVENT_NOT_FOUND`).

Unprocessable.description: A referenced entity does not exist in Akasha (`ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`), or a plotline continuation would loop (`PLOTLINE_CYCLE`).

ETag.description: Current revision, e.g. "3". Echo as If-Match on the next write.

Book.description: A collection of plotlines converging on one terminus event.

overview.example: A smuggler's oath, and the winter it costs her.
overview.description: What this book is about, in the writer's own words. Free prose that no rule reads. Empty string when never written — never null.

terminus.description: Id of the event every plotline must end at.

calendar.description: The primary attachment's descriptor. Kept for clients written before a book could hold several calendars; derived from `calendars`, never stored separately.

world.description: The Akasha database this book's characters, items and locations live in. A default for the article pickers, not a constraint — an EntityRef still names its own database.

plotlines.description: Ids of the plotlines in this book.

status.description: Whether the story-logic checks currently pass. Details via /validate.

calendars.description: Every reckoning this book keeps, in the writer's order. The first is the primary. Several at once are the point: parallel cultures counting one canonical tick line. Choosing between them changes labels only — no tick, no ordering and no verdict moves.

example.title: The Ember Pact
example.overview: Four threads converge on a coronation nobody wants.

BookWrite.description: Writable fields of a book. The id comes from the URL.

overview.description: Free-prose summary. Optional; omitting it stores an empty one. PUT replaces the whole document, so an update that means to keep the existing overview must send it back. At most 10 000 characters.

calendar.description: The pre-library single-calendar spelling, still accepted. Stored as a one-element `calendars` list under the id `default`.

calendars.description: Replaces the whole list. Ids must be unique within the book. Each entry names a library calendar via `source`; a `descriptor` is refused. Send this *or* the older single `calendar`, never both. A book with no calendars shows plain integer ticks — that is how "no calendar" is said, not by describing one inline.

Calendar.description: Optional descriptor that translates between integer ticks and readable dates. Cycles are ordered smallest first and nest over the base unit; their names are the keys a `Date` is written with.

kind.description: Defaults to mixed_radix when cycles are given.

Event.description: One scene: who was there, with what, where, over which timeframe.

start_tick.description: Signed tick; negative is before the epoch. Null when the scene is not scheduled yet.

start_label.description: start_tick formatted by the book's calendar.

scheduled.description: False while the scene has no timing yet. Unscheduled scenes are skipped by conflict and ordering checks.

example.title: The Harbor Exchange
example.description: Aldric and Lyra exchange the Ember Seal beneath the harbour market awnings.

EventWrite.description:
Writable fields of an event. The id comes from the URL. Every EntityRef must already exist in Akasha.

The timeframe may be given as raw `start_tick`/`end_tick` or as `start_date`/`end_date` in the calendar named by `?calendar=` -- never both. Either way: both ends or neither, and omitting them records an unscheduled scene, which a drafting writer can time later.

start_tick.description: Omit or null to leave the scene unscheduled. Must be paired with end_tick, and not combined with start_date/end_date.

end_tick.description: Must be >= start_tick, and paired with it.

start_date.description: Takes the first tick of the period it names. Paired with end_date.

end_date.description: Takes the first tick *after* the period it names, so the same date in both fields spans exactly that period.

example.title: Aldric Departs
example.description: Sir Aldric rides out from Highkeep at dawn.

Plotline.description: One thread of a book: an ordered segment of events plus goals. `events` is what is stored; when `continues_into` is set the thread carries on into another plotline, and `effective_events` is the resolved full path every rule is judged on. `status`, `_links`, `rev` and `effective_events` are server-computed (readOnly).

id.description: Plotline id (slug), unique within the book.

title.description: Optional short display name; defaults to id.

overview.example: Mara's thread: the debt she takes on, and who pays it.
overview.description: What this thread is about, in the writer's own words. Free prose that no rule reads. Empty string when never written — never null.

events.description: This plotline's OWN segment, as stored -- ordered event ids. Send this back on a write.

rev.description: Optimistic-concurrency counter; echo as If-Match on write.

continues_into.description: Id of the plotline this thread continues into, so a shared ending is stored once. Null when the thread carries its own full path.

continues_into_title.description: Display title of the `continues_into` target, so a client can name the thread rather than showing its slug. Null when there is no continuation -- and when the target does not exist, which `status.continuation` reports rather than this field papering over.

continues_into_at.description: Scene on the continuation's resolved path where this thread joins it. Null means its first scene. Lets a thread catch the trunk partway down without copying the trunk's opening into its own `events`.

effective_events.description: The resolved full path: own segment followed by the continuation chain. Bare ids by default; EventSummary objects when ?expand=events.

example.title: The Knight's Road
example.overview: Aldric carries the seal north, and learns what it is for.

PlotlineWrite.description: Writable fields of a plotline. The id comes from the URL. Referenced events must exist in the same book.

overview.description: Free-prose summary. Optional; omitting it stores an empty one. PUT replaces the whole document, so an update that means to keep the existing overview must send it back. At most 10 000 characters.

events.description: Ordered event ids -- this plotline's own segment.

continues_into.description: Another plotline in the same book to continue into. Must exist, and must not create a loop (422 PLOTLINE_CYCLE).

continues_into_at.description: Where to join `continues_into`: a scene on that thread's resolved path, or null for its first. Requires `continues_into`, and the scene must be on its path (400 INVALID_PLOTLINE).

PlotlineStatus.description: Computed verdicts for this plotline (soft model: reported, not blocking). Never accepted on write.

conflicts.description: How many distinct problems this thread has on its effective path (temporal conflicts, ordering violations, scenes with no possible time). A pair problem counts once; informational hints are not counted. Per-scene detail is in `effective_events[].findings` (with `?expand=events`).

Verdict.description: The shared 'finding' shape for a single rule. On `ok`, only `state` is present; on `conflicted`, the rest describe and locate the problem.

code.description: Stable machine code, e.g. ORDERING_VIOLATION, TERMINUS_VIOLATION.

evidence.description: Structured pointer to the offending elements.

doc.description: Deep link to the governing design section.

Span.description: The tick range covered by the plotline, with codec-formatted labels. Null when the plotline has no resolvable events.

EventSummary.description: An event as inlined by ?expand=events, annotated in this plotline's context.

title.description: Optional short display name; defaults to id.

start_tick.description: Signed tick; negative is before the epoch. Null when the scene is not scheduled yet.

start_parts.description: The start label pre-split into coarse-to-fine components (one per calendar cycle, then the clock+epoch); null when unscheduled. Lets a UI group by period without parsing the string.

end_parts.description: The end label pre-split into coarse-to-fine components (one per calendar cycle, then the clock+epoch); null when unscheduled. Lets a UI group by period without parsing the string.

description_preview.description: Truncated body; full text via GET .../events/{id}.

shared_with.description: Other plotlines that also contain this event (convergence/divergence).

is_convergence.description: More than one thread merges into this event (in-degree > 1).

is_divergence.description: More than one thread splits out of this event (out-degree > 1).

scheduled.description: False while the scene has no timing yet. Unscheduled scenes are skipped by conflict and ordering checks.

owned.description: Whether this scene sits in the plotline's own stored `events` segment. False for a scene inherited through `continues_into`: it belongs to the plotline it is stored on, so an edit must be routed there.

findings.description: What is wrong (or merely worth knowing) about this scene on this thread. Soft: findings are reported, never blocking (design 8.1).

ValidateReport.description: Every story-logic check across the whole book. Empty arrays and `convergence.ok` mean the story holds together.

temporal_conflicts.description: Characters in two different places at overlapping times.

ordering.description: Plotlines whose events are not in non-overlapping order.

missing_entities.description: Scenes pointing at articles that have since been deleted.

unscheduled.description: Scenes still waiting for timing — a to-do list, not a fault: these alone do not make a book conflicted. Each carries the window its neighbours imply; an `impossible` window IS a contradiction.

temporal_conflicts.message: 'aldric-at-emberport' and 'aldric-departs' place a character in two places at once.

ConflictFinding.description: One temporal conflict. `evidence.events`, `locations` and `ticks` are positionally paired.

ConvergenceReport.description: Whether every plotline ends at the terminus. Vacuously ok for a book with no plotlines.

Graph.description: The union of every plotline's ordering. Acyclic by construction, since ticks increase along every edge.

convergence.description: Event ids with in-degree > 1 (more than one distinct predecessor).

divergence.description: Event ids with out-degree > 1 (more than one distinct successor).

plotlines.description: One lane per thread, name-ordered. Carries the stored own segment and continues_into alongside the resolved effective path, so a client can draw lanes and a future editor can route edits to the right stored field.

GraphNode.description: An event as a graph node, with its timing and its role in the story graph, so a client can lay it out by tick and colour it by role.

start_parts.description: The start label pre-split into coarse-to-fine components (one per calendar cycle, then the clock+epoch); null when unscheduled. Lets a UI group by period without parsing the string.

end_parts.description: The end label pre-split into coarse-to-fine components; null when unscheduled.

GraphPlotline.description: A thread as a lane in the story graph.

events.description: The thread's stored own segment (before continuation resolution).

effective_events.description: The resolved path: own segment followed by the continuation chain.

GraphEdge.description: A 'precedes' edge, carrying every plotline that traverses it.

EventNeighborhood.description: Which plotlines pass through, converge into, and diverge out of a single event. Built for reading: ids carry titles, times are codec-formatted, and `role`/`summary` state what is happening. All fields are computed by the presenter — nothing here is stored.

role.description: One-word graph role of the event.

through.description: Every plotline that contains this event.

converging.description: Threads arriving at the event, grouped by the predecessor they come from (sorted by predecessor start_tick).

is_convergence.description: True when entered by more than one distinct predecessor edge.

diverging.description: Threads leaving the event, grouped by the successor they go to (sorted by successor start_tick).

is_divergence.description: True when left toward more than one distinct successor.

is_origin.description: True when no plotline has an event before this one (a starting point).

example.summary: Convergence point: threads merge here from 2 prior events.

EdgeGroup.description: The plotlines sharing one neighboring event. `from` is set on incoming groups, `to` on outgoing groups.

NodeRef.description: A readable reference to an event: id plus display title, codec-formatted time, and (optionally) location name.

PlotlineRef.description: A readable reference to a plotline: id plus display title.

Collaborator.description: A user's role on one book.

Role.description: Preset over the shared permission model: reader=read, editor=read+write, owner=read+write+delete.

EntityRef.description: A reference to a document in Akasha that MUST exist (character, item, or location).

Links.description: Discoverable next actions for this resource.

Finding.description: Error envelope — the same vocabulary as a Verdict, so one shape covers errors, status verdicts and /validate entries.

example.error: One or more referenced entities do not exist.

Window.description: Where an unscheduled scene could go, inferred from its plotline neighbours. Null on a side means unconstrained. `impossible` means the surrounding scenes leave no room at all — a real contradiction.

Article.description: A referenced Akasha article, read back through Chronos for display. `document` is the article's flat body (`title`, `body`, plus arbitrary infobox facts).

PlotlineRow.description: One plotline as shown in the visualiser's table.

name.description: Display name (title, or id when untitled).

overview.description: The thread's free-prose summary, shown under its name. Also matched by the `filter` parameter.

conflicts.description: How many distinct problems this thread has on its effective path (temporal conflicts, ordering violations, scenes with no possible time). A pair problem counts once. 0 means it holds together.

PlotlinePage.description: One page of a book's plotlines, filtered by word and ordered by name.

pages.description: Total pages at this page size (>= 1).

Issue.description: One problem in a book. Folded across every thread that can see it: a pair problem reported on both scenes, and on each thread either scene sits on, is one issue here.

severity.description: `conflict` is a contradiction to fix; `info` is worth knowing but not a fault.

message.description: Written for the novelist, not the machine.

scene.description: The scene the message is said about ("this scene has not ended when …"). Null for a book-wide issue such as no ending being designated.

plotlines.description: Every thread this lands on. Empty for a book-wide issue, and for a scene no thread lists.

refs.description: The Akasha articles this message quotes, by id — a client holding the grant may substitute each title for the quoted `'id'`.

IssueGroup.description: Issues of one kind, under the heading they are filed beneath.

title.description: The heading, e.g. "Scenes out of order".

severity.description: Shared by every issue in the group — severity follows the code and a group is one heading's worth of codes, so it is stated once here rather than repeated on each entry.

codes.description: The codes filed under it; more than one where two codes share a heading.

BookReport.description: Everything wrong across one book's plotlines, grouped for reading.

status.description: Conflicted when there is at least one problem. Agrees with the book's own `status`.

unscheduled.description: Of those notes, how many are scenes still waiting for a time.

plotlines.description: Every thread in the book and its share of the problems — the report's triage list and its filter menu, without a second request.

issues.message: This scene has not ended when 'The Harbor Exchange' begins.

notes.title: Scenes still waiting for a time

issues.message: No timing yet — its neighbours put it between 10 and 20.

Permissions.description: What the caller may do with this book, so a UI can decide what to offer before the writer clicks it. Returned by `GET /books/{book}` only.

write.description: May create and edit plotlines and events.

EventFinding.description: One thing worth saying about one scene on one thread. The same rules as `/validate`, attributed to the scene the writer should look at.

severity.description: `conflict` is a contradiction to fix; `info` is a hint (e.g. the window an undated scene must fall inside).

message.description: Written for the novelist, not the machine.

events.description: Other scenes involved. A pair problem is reported on both scenes, phrased from each one's point of view.

refs.description: The Akasha articles this message quotes, by id. Their titles live in Akasha and the reader may not hold a grant on them, so the message uses ids; a client that can read an article may substitute its title for the quoted `'id'`.

example.message: 'The Harbor Exchange' has not ended when this scene begins.

EventRow.description: One scene as offered by the editor's picker.

title.description: Display name (title, or id when untitled).

when.description: Human timeframe: a label, a span, or 'unscheduled'.

location.description: Id of the location article. Compact, and what the `filter` parameter matches; use `location_ref` to resolve its title.

plotlines.description: Plotlines whose effective path already contains this scene.

EventPage.description: One page of a book's scenes, filtered by word and ordered by time (undated scenes last).

pages.description: Total pages at this page size (>= 1).

PlotlinePreview.description: A candidate plotline to judge without saving it. Same fields as PlotlineWrite, plus the id it would be saved under. `goals` may be omitted while drafting -- they feed no rule.

id.description: The plotline being edited, or the id a new one will take. Omit for an unnamed draft.

events.description: Ordered event ids -- the candidate's own segment. Must exist in the book.

EntityCandidate.description: One Akasha article the picker offers, already filtered to what the caller may read.

title.description: The article's title, or its id when untitled.

EntitySuggestions.description: Type-ahead results for the article picker, plus the scope they were read from.

database.description: The Akasha database searched: the one this book's scenes mostly reference, or the book id when it has none yet.

collections.description: Collections this book's existing scenes reference in that database, so a picker can offer them.

PlotlinePreviewResult.description: A candidate plotline, presented by the same code that presents a stored one -- which is the point: the editor's live feedback and the eventual save cannot disagree. Distinguished by `kind`, and missing `rev`/`_links.self`, because it describes something unsaved.

id.description: The candidate's id, or a stand-in for an unnamed draft.

title.description: Optional short display name; defaults to id.

overview.description: The candidate's free-prose summary, echoed back unchanged.

events.description: This plotline's OWN segment, as stored -- ordered event ids. Send this back on a write.

continues_into.description: Id of the plotline this thread continues into, so a shared ending is stored once. Null when the thread carries its own full path.

continues_into_title.description: Display title of the `continues_into` target, so a client can name the thread rather than showing its slug. Null when there is no continuation -- and when the target does not exist, which `status.continuation` reports rather than this field papering over.

continues_into_at.description: Scene on the continuation's resolved path where this thread joins it. Null means its first scene.

effective_events.description: The resolved full path: own segment followed by the continuation chain. Bare ids by default; EventSummary objects when ?expand=events.

TickLabels.description: What a book's calendar calls a set of ticks, in prose (`label`, `parts`) and in numbers (`components`). The inverse -- turning a date back into ticks -- is `POST /books/{book}/ui/dates`.

parts.description: The label split coarse-to-fine, as in EventSummary.start_parts.

readings.description: The same tick dated in *every* calendar the book keeps, including any that were not being kept then. `label`/`parts` above stay the chosen (or primary) reckoning, so a pre-library client is unaffected.

components.description: The same date as numbers, keyed by the calendar's own unit names -- what a form puts back into its date inputs, and what it would send to `POST /books/{book}/ui/dates` or as an event's `start_date`. Cycles are 1-indexed, the base unit 0-indexed, and the top cycle is open-ended (so `Year 0` and below are the pre-epoch ticks). `null` when there is no date to be had: a plain tick line, a tick outside the era this reckoning was kept for, or a calendar that names two units the same.

MissingEntityFinding.description: A scene naming an Akasha article that no longer exists. Referential integrity is enforced on write, so this can only be an article deleted *after* the scene was written — Akasha holds no back-reference to Chronos and cannot warn anyone at the time.

role.description: The part the missing article played in the scene.

Worlds.description: The Akasha worlds the caller may draw a book's cast from, each with the categories they may read inside it.

CalendarAttachment.description:
One reckoning a book keeps its dates in. A book **names** a library calendar; it cannot describe one of its own. The server reads the descriptor out of the library and copies it in, which is why the copy can never disagree with the entry it claims to come from, why provenance cannot be forged, and why a book can only ever hold a calendar that really exists in somebody's library.

Copying happens **on attach, not on every save** — otherwise editing a book's title would quietly adopt whatever the library had become since. `source.rev` is how a caller chooses: omit it to take the calendar as it stands, or send the revision this book already holds to keep that copy.

id.description: Unique within the book. What `?calendar=` names.

label.description: What the view switcher shows. Falls back to the id.

descriptor.description: Resolved from the library at attach time. Returned on reads; **rejected on writes** — a book that sends one gets a 400.

from_tick.description: When this reckoning began. Ticks are offset by it, so a calendar founded mid-story reads Year 1 at its own start. Null means it has always been kept.

until_tick.description: The first tick *not* covered (half-open, as everywhere else). A scene outside the span formats as “before/after <label>” rather than being given a date in a calendar nobody was keeping — which is how a destroyed culture's calendar stops dating the epilogue.

source.description: The library calendar this attachment takes its content from. Owner-qualified because library ids are unique per writer, not globally.

rev.description: Omit for "take it as it stands" (a fresh attach, or accepting an update). Send the revision this book already holds for "keep mine". The response always carries the revision actually read.

primary.description: Whether a read with no `?calendar=` uses this one. True for the first attachment.

LibraryCalendar.description: A named, reusable calendar in a writer's library. Identity is `(owner, id)`: calendar names are generic enough that two writers will independently pick the same slug, so a global namespace would let whoever registered “imperial” first own that word for everybody — and would tell the next writer that a calendar they cannot read exists. Attaching one to a book copies it; nothing here is on the read path of a book's dates.

qualified_id.description: `owner/id`. What a picker shows when the same name appears twice.

notes.description: Free prose. Empty when never written — never null.

LibraryCalendarWrite.description: Writable fields. The id comes from the URL and the owner from the session. A descriptor is required: “plain numbers” is a book attaching no calendar, not a library entry.

example.name: Imperial Reckoning
example.notes: Kept in the capital from the Founding onwards.

CalendarLibrary.description: Every calendar the caller may read: their own, plus any shared with them.

CollaboratorList.description: Everyone granted access at exactly this scope, including the owner. Sorted by username.

ThreadRollup.description: One thread, with how many of this report's problems name it. Not the same number as `PlotlineRow.conflicts`: that counts contradictions among the scenes on a thread, while this also counts the whole-thread verdicts (never reaching the ending, no scenes at all) which the table never shows.

Date.description:
A date, keyed by this calendar's own unit names (see `Calendar.cycles` and `base_unit`; `TickLabels.components` is the same shape coming back). Cycles are 1-indexed, the base unit 0-indexed, and the top cycle is open-ended.

Components must run contiguously from the largest unit down -- `{year, month}` is a date, a bare `{day}` is not. Omitting the finer ones is how a date names a **period**: `{year: 3, month: 4, day: 12}` is the whole of that day. A `start_date` takes the period's first tick and an `end_date` the first tick after it, so the same date in both fields spans exactly that day.

DateQuery.description: A timeframe to resolve. Accepts exactly what `EventWrite` accepts -- dates or ticks, both ends or neither -- and applies the same rules, so a timeframe this endpoint accepts is one the save will accept.

ResolvedDates.description: The ticks a timeframe resolves to, plus those ticks dated back again -- so a form can echo the reading it is about to save without a second round trip. `ticks` omits an end that was not given.

end_tick.description: Exclusive, as everywhere else: the first tick after the scene.

parts.description: The label split coarse-to-fine, as in EventSummary.start_parts.

readings.description: The same tick dated in *every* calendar the book keeps, including any that were not being kept then. `label`/`parts` above stay the chosen (or primary) reckoning, so a pre-library client is unaffected.

components.description: The same date as numbers, keyed by the calendar's own unit names -- what a form puts back into its date inputs, and what it would send to `POST /books/{book}/ui/dates` or as an event's `start_date`. Cycles are 1-indexed, the base unit 0-indexed, and the top cycle is open-ended (so `Year 0` and below are the pre-epoch ticks). `null` when there is no date to be had: a plain tick line, a tick outside the era this reckoning was kept for, or a calendar that names two units the same.
